messages:
incident-bot: ALERT — model-family=solstice-12b RPM spike detected (3.4x baseline). Backend queue pressure >90%, avg evicted requests rising. Auto-mitigation recommended. thread_ts=2060123456
Maya (oncall): I'm on it. Paging SRE. Tagging @Ravi @Eli. Any immediate customer-facing impact known?
Ravi K: looking at logs now. I'm seeing sustained hotshard on rack-gpu-7 and rack-gpu-9. Token service latency climbing, throttles increasing.
Tess (runtime): Confirmed. KV cache hit stable but worker queue latency exploding. If we don't shape traffic, we'll see OOM evictions on a subset of hosts. Recommend temporary per-model rate cap to reduce incoming RPM (limit user-level burst).
Maya (oncall): What numbers do we want to run to start?
Tess (runtime): Propose immediate RPM=30, TPM=450 for solstice-12b globally. That should cut inbound pressure ~45% based on current distribution. We'll monitor tail latency.
Ravi K: +1 to conservative cut. Also suggest enabling the lite fallback routing for non-enterprise orgs so they get degraded-but-available behavior.
Maya (oncall): Executing mitigation now. /run playbook rate-limit set model=solstice-12b rpm=30 tpm=450 scope=global reason="surge mitigation — hotshard" initiated by Maya (oncall)
deploy-bot: Playbook started by Maya (oncall). Steps: 1) push quota update to config-store, 2) propagate to routing layer, 3) broadcast metrics to dashboard, 4) run smoke checks.
deploy-bot: Step 1 complete — quota entry written to config-store (version 20260315-1432).
Tess (runtime): Step 2 applied. Runtime nodes have new quota; token accounting enforced at ingress. Immediate p95 latency dropping reported. Early metrics: p95 token latency 780ms -> 210ms; queue depth down ~60%.
Eli P: After the change, observed QPS for solstice-12b down ~42%. Error 429 rate up for a small subset of heavy batch customers — looks localized. Which customers are hitting 429s?
Nora (product): Telemetry shows spikes of 429s for acme-inc (customer-id: 42) and dataforge (customer-id: 77). Both are on low-priority plans and were using high-rate batch jobs. Notifying account teams.
Maya (oncall): Noted impacted customers: acme-inc, dataforge. Posting a temporary advisory to the status page: "We are currently applying rate limiting to model family solstice-12b to protect service health. Some batch workloads may receive 429s; please retry with exponential backoff or use the solstice-12b-lite fallback." :warning:
Ravi K: I've enabled fallback routing for non-enterprise customers to solstice-12b-lite. This should absorb some lost requests and reduce 429s.
Tess (runtime): Sharing a quick config snippet applied (for audit):
```yaml
rate_limits:
  solstice-12b:
    rpm: 30
    tpm: 450
    scope: global
    reason: "surge mitigation"
```
Maya (oncall): Monitoring window 15m. If stable, we'll try incremental relaxation for non-latency-sensitive routes.
Eli P: Seeing stabilization at 10m mark. p95 steady ~220ms, CPU across affected hosts normalized. 429s for acme-inc decreased after fallback enable.
Nora (product): Account teams notified. Acme is asking for rough ETA to restore baseline. I told them we'll assess in 1 hour and prioritize paid customers.
Ravi K: Plan for next steps: 1) keep current cap for 30m, 2) if p95 < 300ms and queue depth <20%, increase RPM to 60 for dedicated/paid orgs only, 3) after 2h, consider full restore.
Maya (oncall): Initiating controlled ramp for paid tenants now: /run playbook rate-limit adjust model=solstice-12b rpm=60 scope=paid-tenants comment="controlled ramp after stabilization"
deploy-bot: Adjustment applied for scope=paid-tenants. Monitoring for error spikes.
Tess (runtime): No regressions seen in the last 5m. Will keep close eye on hotshard signals and KV eviction rates.
Maya (oncall): Handoff to SRE shift B: @Eli, please pick up monitoring and customer comms for the next hour. I'll add a short incident summary and next steps.
Eli P: Acknowledged — taking over. Will escalate if token latency or queue pressure rises above thresholds.
Maya (oncall): Summary for handoff (copied to incident channel): 1) Root cause: sudden spike in solstice-12b request fanout causing hotshards on rack-gpu-7/9. 2) Mitigation: global RPM/TMP cap (30/450) + fallback routing for non-paid customers. 3) Customer impact: transient 429s for batch users (acme-inc, dataforge). 4) Next steps: staged relaxation for paid tenants, monitor 2h, review traffic patterns and identify offending clients.
incident-bot: INCIDENT — mitigation in place. Tags: rate-limit, model-family, oncall-handoff.
Eli P: I'll watch for 1h. If all stable, we'll schedule post-incident review tomorrow to consider autoscaling rules and better per-org burst controls.
Maya (oncall): Thanks team :thumbsup: — handing off.
deploy-bot: Playbook completed at 2060123512. All steps successful.
